messages.subject: Feature request: Wrap facets around a circle
messages.subject_clean: Feature request: Wrap facets around a circle
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Would it be possible to wrap facets around a circle, instead of on a linear grid, as in CIRCOS output?  I feel like this is something that should be doable using ggplot, but isn't currently.

Thank you,
Brendan

messages.subject: Re: Feature request: Wrap facets around a circle
messages.subject_clean: Feature request: Wrap facets around a circle
messages.body_plain:
Dear Brendan,

> Would it be possible to wrap facets around a circle, instead of on a
> linear grid, as in CIRCOS output?  I feel like this is something that
> should be doable using ggplot, but isn't currently.

I had a quick look at CIRCOS on line, not being familiar with it.

There seem to be a number of different circular graphics presented
on their web site, so you might want to be more specific with your
query.

However, some of them may be achievable using coord_polar, which
puts the x-axis on a polar coordinates scale and is how, eg, ggplot
can be used to generate a pie chart. This seems much more like
what you want to do than 'wrap facets around a circle'.

I would suggest giving something a go, creating some kind of
reproducible example and raising a query on community.rstudio.com <http://community.rstudio.com>
forums which are far more active than this mailing list these days.

Regards,
Ron.

messages.subject: Re: split/discontinuous axis?
messages.body_plain: This is a very old thread, but I am searching for a solution to this same problem.  Here is my use case: I am a pharmacologist, and I need to plot dose-effects. It is accepted practice to have a discontinuous x-axis in order to break the continuity between the vehicle and active doses.  The reason being that vehicle does not conform to the axis label (e.g. Drug Dose (mg/kg), as it is not a dose of Drug) and does not really represent the position it occupies on the axis (because doses are typically plotted on a log-transformed axis and so vehicle - essentially ZERO dose - has no transformation or position on the axis).

messages.subject: Connecting dodged points with lines based on a grouping
messages.subject_clean: Connecting dodged points with lines based on a grouping
messages.body_plain:
In the following self-contained example, I am trying to connect the "left" and "right" measurements for each patient across the dodge by "measurement". I am close but can't quite get it to work. Any clues?

Thanks!

library("tidyverse")

data <- tibble(patient = seq(1,12,1),
               treatment = rep(c("A","B","C"), each=4),
               left = c(1.2,1.5,2.3,1.1,0.2,0.4,0.6,1.0,0.1,0.5,1.9,1.0),
               right = c(1.1,1.4,1.8,0.9,1.2,1.3,1.5,0.9,1.0,2.0,1.7,2.9)) %>%
    gather(side, measurement, -patient, -treatment)

plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x=treatment, y=measurement)) +
    geom_point(aes(color=side), position=position_dodge(width=0.75)) +
    geom_line(aes(group=patient), position=position_dodge(width=0.75))

print(plot)
ggsave("plot.jpg", plot)
